newsitem.title: CHINA: China to end monopoly on trade in six commodities.
newsitem.headline: China to end monopoly on trade in six commodities.

text.p: China plans to loosen state controls on import rights for six commodities as part of efforts to gain entry to the World Trade Organization (WTO), state media and officials said on Monday.

Over the next three years more domestic enterprises would be allowed to import rubber, steel, wood, wool, acrylic fibre and plywood -- six of 12 commodities handled as state monopolies or semi-monopolies, the Overseas Edition of People's Daily said. "This is still an issue in WTO consultations between China and WTO member nations and (the loosening of controls) cannot be implemented immediately," said an official of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.
He declined to give further details.
China would retain controls on imports of the other six commodities, which were wheat, crude oil, oil products, fertiliser, cotton and tobacco, the newspaper said.
